walkthroughs.body_html:
Theme C: The Existence of God & Revelation — a core area of GCSE Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Theme C: The Existence of God & Revelation brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Theme C: The Existence of God & Revelation.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What does the design argument conclude?
options: Order and purpose in nature point to a designer - God
The universe has no order
God cannot be known at all
Design proves the universe is eternal

mcqs.q: In the First Cause argument, God is described as what?
options: The uncaused cause that brought the universe into existence
The final event of the universe
A being caused by the Big Bang
One cause among many equal causes
God revealed indirectly to everyone, for example through nature and scripture
A vision granted to one person
A message given only to priests
A miracle performed in private

mcqs.q: What did Hume argue about miracles?
options: Testimony for a miracle is never strong enough to outweigh the evidence for the laws of nature
Miracles happen every day
Only ancient miracles are reliable
Science has confirmed most miracles

mcqs.q: Does accepting the Big Bang force someone to reject belief in God?
options: Visions are accepted only if they happen in a place of worship.
No - many believers accept the Big Bang and argue God is the cause behind it, while atheists see no need for a cause beyond nature; the science itself does not settle the question.
The Big Bang is a religious doctrine found in Genesis.
The Big Bang theory disproves the existence of God.

mcqs.q: Did evolution end every form of the design argument?
options: Not for everyone - evolution challenges Paley-style examples of designed organisms, but some believers relocate design to the laws and fine-tuning of the universe; the debate continues.
Evolution was proposed as an argument for God's existence.
Darwin's theory made all design arguments impossible to hold.
Visions are accepted only if they happen in a place of worship.

mcqs.q: Do religious believers accept every claimed vision as genuine revelation?
options: Religions automatically believe anyone who says they have seen God.
No - traditions test claims against scripture, teaching and their effects on the person's life; many claimed revelations are rejected as mistaken or fraudulent.
Visions are accepted only if they happen in a place of worship.
Evolution was proposed as an argument for God's existence.
